spec.name: reference
spec.why: Noiseless, moderate ellipticity, interpolation everywhere. The configuration the acceptance criterion is evaluated on.

spec.name: eps_circular
spec.why: Near-circular rings, where sampling differences between the tools are smallest.

spec.name: eps_high
spec.why: Strong ellipticity. The ring statistic each tool forms differs most here, and the secant is a difference of two such statistics.

spec.name: pa_30
spec.why: A gradient is a scalar and should not care about orientation. A null result that would expose a sampling asymmetry if it were not one.

spec.name: interpolate_default
spec.why: AutoProf's default sampling. Nearest-pixel rounding perturbs b0 itself, so it perturbs a difference of two b0 values -- possibly more than it perturbs either.

spec.name: background_offset
spec.why: A constant cancels exactly in a difference, so every reconstructed gradient must be unchanged. The sharpest null test on this grid.

spec.name: noise_snr100
spec.why: A secant differences two noisy ring means over a short baseline, which amplifies noise relative to either mean. This is where the reconstruction is expected to hurt.

spec.name: noise_snr30
spec.why: Harder noise, and the case that decides whether the reconstruction survives realistic data or only clean fixtures.

licensing.withdrawn_criterion_2: The original criterion 2 (bender <= raw + gradient) was withdrawn on 2026-08-23. Bender is constructed from raw and gradient, so the comparison is an arithmetic identity check rather than independent evidence; it also compared maxima from different rings and added percentage errors linearly where the exact bound carries a denominator. It survives as the 'algebraic_consistency' diagnostic.
